title: Retrieval Metrics
text: Retrieval quality measures whether a search system finds relevant source documents. Precision measures the proportion of retrieved documents that are relevant. Recall measures the proportion of all relevant documents retrieved. Mean reciprocal rank rewards systems that place the first relevant result near the top. Normalized discounted cumulative gain rewards relevant results at higher ranks. BM25 is a lexical ranking method based on term frequency and inverse document frequency.

title: Grounded Generation
text: Grounded generation uses retrieved source context to produce answers. A grounded answer should be supported by evidence and avoid unsupported claims. Citation coverage measures how often answer statements include references. Groundedness evaluation can use human review, model judges, or automated heuristics. Lexical overlap cannot establish semantic entailment.

title: RAG Operations
text: Reliable retrieval augmented generation requires repeatable evaluation datasets, versioned configurations, monitoring, and regression tests. Teams compare retrieval metrics across experiments and investigate quality regressions before deployment. Chunk size and overlap influence recall, context precision, latency, and token usage. A release gate can block deployment when quality metrics fall below thresholds.

title: Knowledge Base Security
text: Knowledge base ingestion should validate file types and payload sizes, sanitize untrusted content, and enforce access control at retrieval time. Retrieved documents are untrusted data. Secrets and private customer information should not be added to public benchmark datasets. Logs should avoid storing sensitive prompts or documents without an approved retention policy.
